one_line: A 2 min 20 s sponsored talking-head video where the presenter explains why 'be nice to your sister' fails and gives parents one sentence to say after watching a sibling-themed show (Gabby's Dollhouse) together, closing on a guilt-free screen time reassurance.

hook.visual: Woman in a brown knit top at a wooden desk with dark shelves and books behind her, shot waist-up straight to camera; a white rounded title box above bold word-by-word captions.
hook.on_screen_text: How to Reduce Sibling Arguments (Without Saying "Be Nice") (title box, visible at 0.0 and 3.12 s) plus burned-in caption "What if I told you"
hook.first_spoken_line: What if I told you that watching a TV show with your kids, the thing that you feel a little guilty about, can help with sibling fights? (Whisper)
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: Inferred: it flips a common parent guilt (screen time) into a benefit for a very common pain (sibling fights) and the title box names the pain and the forbidden phrase in the first second.

beats.observed: Presenter mid-speech at the desk; white title box then burned-in captions; hand gestures; a close crop at about 9 s.
beats.spoken: What if I told you that watching a TV show with your kids ... can help with sibling fights? Now stay with me.
beats.on_screen_text: How to Reduce Sibling Arguments (Without Saying "Be Nice")

beats.observed: Tighter crop at 9.4 s with a scrunched face as she imitates the parent line; hand wave at 12.5 s.
beats.spoken: Be nice to your sister! We all say that ... we all know it doesn't really work.

beats.observed: Wide shot with open-hand gestures; at 28.1 s both hands form a barrier shape in front of the chest while she says 'blocker'; captions word by word.
beats.spoken: Your kid already has kindness inside them. When they're not being nice, something's blocking access to it. Jealousy. Anger. ... Be nice skips over all that.
beats.on_screen_text: caption words only ("blocking access", "as a blocker", "Be nice", "effective.")

beats.observed: Alternating wide and close-up angles with open-hand gestures; at 46.8 and 50.0 s she turns slightly off-axis in a tight crop.
beats.spoken: The right TV show, yes TV, can actually be used as an effective tool ... we do something we call a side door. And a show gives you the side door.
beats.on_screen_text: caption words only ("can actually", "We do something", "and a show")

beats.observed: At 53.1 s a small Gabby's Dollhouse poster (Netflix, September 14) pops over her torso; cutaways at 56 to 66 s show a live-action girl with a decorated frozen banana pop, then in a chef hat with a bowl, then a talking clip.
beats.spoken: In the new season of Gabby's Dollhouse we meet Gabby's little sister, Doozy ... they're making frozen bananas ... when Doozy slams the door ... Gabby just smiles and says, "I love my sister."

beats.observed: Back to the presenter in alternating wide and tight crops; at 87.4 s both hands are extended palms down as she says to leave it at that.
beats.spoken: Watch it together. And then afterward, in a low stakes kind of way, say something simple and short. Like, hmm, sometimes a little sister can feel so good, and sometimes I bet it feels so hard. I bet Gabby feels mad at Doozy sometimes. Leave it at that.
beats.on_screen_text: caption "kind of way." / "and short," / "feel so good," / "feels so hard." / "at Doozie"

beats.observed: She voices the child, grimacing, at 93.7 to 96.8 s; hands held close to the chest at 99.9 s.
beats.spoken: Do not expect a profound reply. 'Wow, Mom, just like me and my sibling.' Won't happen. You're probably going to get silence, or 'can I have a snack?' Still, it landed. It matters. I promise.
beats.on_screen_text: caption "a profound" / "and my sibling!" / "Or can I have" / "It matters,"

beats.observed: Direct address with intense facial expressions, a fist gesture at 112.4 s for 'a hit'.
beats.spoken: Now your kid knows it's okay to feel mad ... love and frustration at a sibling at the same time ... less likely to come out as a hit or a tease ... all because you watched a TV episode and used it as a side [cut off].
beats.on_screen_text: caption "okay" / "and frustration" / "or mad" / "as a hit or" / "behavior." / "and used it"

beats.observed: Final stretch with only burned-in captions and gestures; no end card or logo seen in sampled frames to 137.4 s.
beats.spoken: No usable transcript after about 2:00 (Whisper stops mid-sentence).
beats.on_screen_text: caption "emotional world." / "that has" / "real life," / "on the back." / "because you" / "to connect" (inferred closing: let go of the guilt, per the post caption)

payoff: The sayable line to use after the show arrives at about 1:15 to 1:27 (75 to 87 s); the emotional payoff (it is okay to feel mad, love and frustration can coexist) at about 1:42 to 2:00; the guilt-release close at about 2:00 to 2:20 is inferred from captions and the post text.
cta: No explicit follow, share or comment ask observed. The closing message (per the post caption) is permission-giving: next time you put on a show, let go of the guilt.
share_or_comment_trigger: A forwardable script (exact sentence to say), an expectation reset ('you might get silence or a snack request') and permission to stop feeling guilty about screens. 476 shares versus only 22 comments (shares far outweigh comments).
why_it_worked: 76,400 views vs account median 5,056.5 (15.1x); the hook turns screen-time guilt into a benefit for a very common problem, and the title box names the pain in the first second.

like_rate 4.85% (3,703 likes) and 476 shares are far above the 0.3% paid flag, so the engagement is organic for a sponsored post; a verbatim sentence plus 'don't expect a reply' makes it feel doable and save-worthy.

At 140 s it only works if pacing holds: alternating wide and tight angles every few seconds, word-by-word captions and a built-in tease ('side door') delay the payoff to about 75 s (retention data not provided, so this is inferred).
paid_signal: no for boosted views: like_rate 4.85% and 476 shares are well above the 0.3% flag. Separately, the caption carries #NetflixPartner, so this is a disclosed sponsored partnership (observed in caption), but sponsored content is not the same as paid reach.

solo_route.how: 1) Recruit a barter child psychologist or parenting educator and give them a skeleton to deliver in 90 to 120 s: a contrarian hook, why the usual phrase fails, a 'side door' object, the one sentence to say, and the 'don't expect a reply' reassurance. 2) Film on a phone at a desk with shelves behind, 9:16, eye level, one long take recorded twice in two framings (wide and tight); in CapCut punch in every 3 to 5 s, add word-by-word auto captions in bold white and a white rounded title box for the first 5 s. 3) Use LumeBook's own AI illustrations (a child hero with a sibling) as the inset visual in place of licensed TV clips, with consent from any real family. 4) End on a permission line, then the LumeBook handle.
solo_route.needs: A barter expert who owns all psychology claims and approves the script; consent if a real family's photo is used for the illustration.

lumebook_version.hook_he: 'תהיה נחמד לאחות שלך' לא עובד. הנה למה
lumebook_version.concept: A barter child psychologist explains why the usual sibling phrase fails and uses a LumeBook story (child hero with a sibling) as the 'side door': read it together, then say one soft sentence about feelings. Wide and tight cuts, burned-in Hebrew captions, no product pitch until the end.

evidence_notes: Observed: the title box, desk setting, alternating wide and tight framings across sampled frames (cuts inferred from this, frames are 3.1 s apart), the Gabby's Dollhouse poster at 53.1 s, live-action show cutaways at 56 to 66 s, burned-in captions through 137.4 s. Spoken: Whisper English is quite clean and matches the on-screen captions, but the SRT stops at about 1:59.96 mid-sentence although the video runs 140 s, so the last ~20 s rely on visible caption fragments and the post caption (inferred). Spelling 'Doozie' is from the captions; Whisper wrote 'Doozy'. The presenter is not identified beyond the account name. Show footage ownership and claims about the show's benefit are not verified. No retention data. Sampling step is 3.12 s so short cutaways may be missed.
